scope: Whole-setup monthly power planning, not independently measured wall-power results. Hardware stays awake with models loaded; displays off/dim, batteries charged, and no external peripherals or other workloads.
monthly_method: Active benchmark watts plus active_overhead_watts apply only to utilized hours. idle_watts is the entire idle setup and applies only to remaining hours. Do not add idle watts again to the active total.
active_energy_columns: Retain original benchmark scope and exclude idle and the separate monthly host allowance.
limits: H200 idle GPU draw of 180 W is measured by the user; its 100 W host allowance is an estimate.
GPU-only active figures omit components that can change under load; the added host allowances are approximate, not calibrated whole-machine measurements.
Idle power and active host allowances are fixed properties of the selected hardware and are labeled as estimates.
Utilization is a time fraction, not GPU utilization percentage, batch size, or a throughput multiplier from concurrency.

records.basis: 180 W combined GPU idle draw measured by the user, plus an estimated 100 W host allowance. Monthly active power adds the same 100 W host allowance to the measured 400 W GPU total. Host power is unverified.

source_anchors.note: Two GPUs at 90 W each. Host power is not measured; 100 W is an independent planning allowance.

records.basis: Estimated whole desktop idle draw: approximately 30 W GPU plus 30 W for CPU, RAM, storage, fans and power losses. Loaded-model idle was not measured on this desktop.

source_anchors.note: Review reports about 33 W GPU-only idle. A 30 W GPU plus 30 W host budget gives the 60 W whole-desktop assumption; exact loaded-model idle is not measured.

records.basis: Estimated whole desktop idle draw: approximately 35 W GPU plus 40 W for the rest of the desktop. Published GPU-only desktop-idle tests vary roughly 25–46 W; loaded-model idle was not measured here.

source_anchors.note: Review reports 46 W GPU-only idle with its setup; other reviewed display configurations report around 25–31 W. The 75 W desktop default budgets about 35 W GPU plus 40 W host; it is not a matched measurement.

records.basis: Estimated whole-Mac idle draw, awake with the model loaded. Apple reports 6 W for a smaller 32-GPU-core, 36 GB M4 Max Studio with Finder only; 10 W is a planning allowance for this 40-core, 64 GB configuration.

source_anchors.note: Apple reports 6 W wall idle for a smaller 32-GPU-core, 36 GB M4 Max Studio, Finder only. 10 W allows for the selected larger configuration and loaded runtime; not a measured result.

records.basis: Estimated whole Studio idle draw with model residency. Apple reports 9 W at the wall for the 80-GPU-core, 512 GB configuration with Finder only; 15 W allows for the serving runtime and residency, not measured here.

source_anchors.note: Apple reports 9 W wall idle for 80 GPU cores and 512 GB, Finder only. 15 W is a planning allowance for serving/runtime activity and memory residency.

records.basis: Estimated total for eight awake laptops at 10 W each, with displays off or dim and batteries charged. M3 Max review idle measurements are roughly 5–8 W under light display settings. Monthly active power adds a separate 80 W non-GPU allowance to the GPU compute estimate; neither allowance is measured on this cluster.

source_anchors.note: Review reports 5.2 W minimum idle, 7.91 W at 150 cd/m², and 6.49 W with an external screen (screen energy excluded). Eight times 10 W allows for awake serving processes and residency. This is not a loaded-cluster measurement.
